question: How does BSP actually buy companies?
html:
BSP buys theme-first. It studies a sector, then acquires an anchor company in a banked process. Larger anchors come from sponsor secondaries and smaller ones from founders or partners. Add-ons follow, along with a management reset where the CEO was inherited (BSP acquisition methodology).

Thesis before the target

  • Deal releases present each company as the result of a sector study done in advance. Examples are "over a year" in electrical services before CET and a watch on accounting before Smith + Howard (BSP acquisition methodology).
  • Since 2024 the filter has narrowed to essential services. Punctual Pros, Frontline and CET are non-discretionary. Fair Harbor is the only discretionary consumer bet (BSP acquisition methodology).

Two kinds of seller

Seller typeAnchor deals (entry date)
Sponsor secondary (larger checks)Thomas Scientific from Carlyle (Jan 27, 2022); BPI from Svoboda (Apr 27, 2023); Frontline from BV (Dec 11, 2024)
Founder or partner, first institutional capital (smaller checks)Fair Harbor (Mar 23, 2022); Smith + Howard (Nov 15, 2022); Punctual Pros (Apr 3, 2024); CET (Feb 2025)
  • In secondaries the outgoing sponsor often rolls a minority stake, as Svoboda did at BPI and BV did at Frontline (BSP firm profile).
  • Structures adapt to the sector. At Smith + Howard, BSP invested in the advisory entity while the licensed CPA firm kept attest work (BSP acquisition methodology).

Banked processes, repeat advisers

  • 6 of 7 anchor deals had a named sell-side adviser. Punctual Pros went to "eight finalists."
  • Berenson advised BSP on Thomas, BPI, Frontline and CET. Harris Williams advised on Punctual Pros and Frontline. Morrison Cohen or Greenberg Traurig was counsel on every deal (BSP acquisition methodology).

Management after close

  • Inherited CEOs are replaced at about 13-15 months. Simmons was succeeded by Haas at Thomas, and Naidoo by Britt at Frontline on Jan 27, 2026.
  • Founder CEOs stay. Examples are Sean Taylor, Matt Buckwalter and John Duquette Jr. (BSP acquisition methodology; BSP firm profile).

Capital and add-ons

  • Financing varies. Thomas carries an Apollo/MidCap unitranche maturing December 2027. Fair Harbor shows no debt on the public record (BSP acquisition methodology).
  • The main fund reports $335M sold as of April 2025. The $50-250M check range is unverified. Against $0.9-2.1B rival funds, BSP leans on co-invest and operating credibility (BSP firm profile; Private-equity landscape).
  • BSP states 23 add-ons, and 21 are identified by name. Fair Harbor and Frontline have none (BSP acquisition methodology).

Limits of this view

  • Weights and size bands are inferences from public evidence, not BSP's internal screening criteria (BSP acquisition methodology).
  • Pricing, multiples and hold-period targets are not in the context. Answering those would require BSP investment committee memos and closing models.

Next actions

  • Close the add-on gap. Name the missing Punctual Pros and Smith + Howard acquisitions from deal files.
  • For Punctual Pros, test proprietary outreach to sub-$3M EBITDA shops against auction pipelines. Sila, Gridiron and Watchtower are active in Central PA/NJ (Private-equity landscape).
  • Benchmark the 13-15 month CEO-transition pattern against current secondary-deal diligence plans. This timing is an est.
  • Prioritise New England electrical and energy-efficiency targets for CET before Kohlberg or Huron roll-ups arrive (Private-equity landscape).
